failure_trace: A pull request is opened and an Antigravity review begins execution under concurrency group antigravity-review-<workflow>-<pr>-review.
The PR author edits the pull request title or body, emitting a pull_request event with action 'edited' where github.event.changes contains only title or body keys.
The runner evaluates the concurrency group at line 13 and the job guard at line 18, attempting to evaluate github.event.changes.base.ref.from != ''.
Because changes.base is undefined, dereferencing yields null, which GitHub Actions compares against '' via numeric coercion (0 != NaN), evaluating to true.
The job condition evaluates to true, triggering a redundant review execution, while the concurrency group resolves to 'review' instead of github.run_id, prematurely canceling the in-progress review.
findings.title: PR title and body edits trigger review runs and cancel active reviews due to flawed retarget expression

findings.body: In `.github/workflows/antigravity-review.yml` at line 18 (and line 13), the condition `(github.event.action != 'edited' || github.event.changes.base.ref.from != '')` is intended to restrict execution on PR edit events to base-ref retargets while isolating title/body edits to distinct concurrency groups. However, when a PR is edited without changing the base ref (such as modifying the title or description), `github.event.changes.base` is omitted from the webhook payload. In GitHub Actions expression evaluation, dereferencing `changes.base.ref.from` evaluates to `null`. Under GitHub Actions loose scalar coercion rules, `null` coerces to `0` and empty string `''` coerces to `NaN`, causing `null != ''` to evaluate to `true` (`0 != NaN`). Consequently, the expression evaluates to `true` on title and body edits, triggering unnecessary review runs at line 18 and resolving the concurrency group to 'review' instead of `github.run_id` at line 13, which cancels active reviews contrary to the intended retarget-only policy.
failure_trace: A pull request is opened and an Antigravity review begins execution under concurrency group antigravity-review-<workflow>-<pr>-review.
The PR author edits the pull request title or body, emitting a pull_request event with action 'edited' where github.event.changes contains only title or body keys.
The runner evaluates the concurrency group at line 13 and the job guard at line 18, attempting to evaluate github.event.changes.base.ref.from != ''.
Because changes.base is undefined, dereferencing yields null, which GitHub Actions compares against '' via numeric coercion (0 != NaN), evaluating to true.
The job condition evaluates to true, triggering a redundant review execution, while the concurrency group resolves to 'review' instead of github.run_id, prematurely canceling the in-progress review.
findings.title: PR title and body edits trigger review runs and cancel active reviews due to flawed retarget expression

questions: Has hosted GitHub Actions workflow execution been tested against real PR title/description edit webhooks to confirm whether in-progress review runs are canceled?
Are runner negative-enforcement canary tests configured to verify complete exclusion of GitHub credentials from the Bubblewrap review runtime environment?
Will the coordinator script `scripts/antigravity_rollout.clj` be updated centrally to resolve the `changes.base` presence check across all member caller repositories?
structured_output.summary: Reviewed the rollout of the pinned Antigravity reviewer caller (.github/workflows/antigravity-review.yml), planning card (kanban/antigravity-review-rollout.md), session ledger (.ημ/session-mycology/ledger.md), and accountability receipts (receipts.edn). Identified a defect in the workflow's retarget expression across lines 13 and 18, where missing `changes.base` on PR title/body edits evaluates to null, causing `null != ''` to evaluate to true under GitHub Actions loose type coercion. This inadvertently triggers review runs and cancels active reviews across irrelevant PR edits.
